newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean cabinet ministers offer to resign.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean cabinet ministers offer to resign.

text.p: South Korean cabinet ministers on Wednesday offered to resign to give President Kim Young-sam a free hand to carry out a major reshuffle of his administration, an official at the Prime Minister's Office said.
"Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung met the president this morning and told him that all cabinet ministers are ready to step down," he said.

Kim, in a dramatic gesture of contrition to try to salvage his presidency, apologised on Tuesday for a loans scandal that landed a cabinet minister and other close associates behind bars and rocked the nation.
Prosecutors said banks pressured by politicians offered huge loans in return for kickbacks from Hanbo Steel, which racked up $5.8 billion in debts before going under on January 23.
Ruling New Korea Party chairman Lee Hong-koo and other party elders also tendered their resignations on Tuesday.
Kim, a former dissident who battled previous military rulers, took power vowing a clean society but his government is now lurching from one corruption scandal to another.
